Carried from #1551 (removes): Precondition for using these harnesses: derive the temp root from TMPDIR, never the hard-coded /home/claude path. Control: The option removed: running the finder's D3 harness as committed. tools/audit/round8/D3/s1_claimkill.py line 54 sets TMP = /home/claude/audit-r8/tmp/D3-s1 and passes it as TMPDIR, and tools/audit/round8/D3/s1_cachekey.py's plandata arm sets HPO_PLANDATA=/home/claude/audit-r8/tmp/D3-s1/plandata; tools/audit/round8/D3/v1_suite_mutants.py line 33 sets /home/claude/audit-r8/tmp/D3-v1. Those roots existed only in the cloud audit container. On the Mac, mkdir /home/claude is refused (Operation not supported), measured by PR #1551's fix reviewer. The judge ran sed-rewritten copies with the root moved and reproduced the finder's numbers, so the root is incidental to the measurement: the null control is the same harness with only that constant changed. Re-measure: Before trusting any number, point the root at a directory under your own TMPDIR (a sed of the one constant, or an env override), run the harness at your merge base and at your head, and diff the only-root-changed copy against the transport copy to show nothing else moved. Cite the transport path with its sha1 as fixer.md step 3 asks, and disclose the root edit as yours. Carried from #1551 (narrows): Narrowed: an on-disk harness is legitimate only in an otherwise idle tree or under the gate lease, whatever fixer.md says about the lease being for MODE FULL and stress.py only. Prefer in-memory perturbation if your fix touches the harness. Harnesses are not in the tree: restore them from transport commit 6f58e33e as the round-8 register section 'What this commit does not carry' in docs/audit-2026-09.md says, so every tools/audit/round8/D3/... path below resolves. Control: Several finder perturbations edit production or test files on disk in the working tree: tools/audit/round8/D3/s1_claimkill.py rewrites the claim file and appends comment-only edits to source files (lines 85-116) and restores them afterwards; tools/audit/round8/D3/v1_suite_mutants.py writes each mutant into the file (lines 98-108). A concurrent run in the same tree then imports the edited file. The judge measured it: its first D2-s1-01 run overlapped its own D0 ftol edit, and that run was discarded; a clean re-run in an idle tree gave identical numbers, which is the null control separating the contamination from the result. Re-measure: Run each on-disk harness in a worktree that nothing else runs in (not the shared checkout, not a tree another seat's gate is using), or hold the gate lease for the duration with python3 tests/gate_lock.py take --label <seat>. After each run, git status must show the tree clean before you measure anything else there. Carried from the mutation-timeout root cause (branch fix/rca-mutation-timeout, PR #1565): the `mutation` job's wall clock is its baseline plus its slowest worker, and a mutant every driver must see -- a survivor, or the comment-only null control this group adds -- costs one full sweep of the driver net. That branch replaces main()'s serial baseline and the per-worker pool[i::jobs] sweep with drive_baselines and drive_pool, which share the drivers across the worker trees and stop a mutant at its first kill, and it names tests/stress.py in EXCLUSIVE: stress.py times its solves against tests/stress_budgets.json, so it runs with no other driver in flight, in the baseline and for every mutant. Precondition for whichever of the two lands second: (1) the null control is driven through drive_pool on a path that runs every shared driver and collects every kill rather than stopping at the first; (2) its stress.py run goes in drive_pool's exclusive phase like any mutant's, never beside another driver -- a null tree driven outside the pool is a fourth process on a three-worker runner; (3) the job's wall clock is re-measured from a CI log of the merged head against the mutation job's timeout-minutes, on the slower runner class (read stress.py's baseline line), never from a local run. (4) Since #1565's round 3, `--scope changed` draws only sites on lines the diff adds or modifies (`changed_lines`, `drawable`), and a comment-only diff yields an empty pool that passes before any baseline. The null control is the tool's own comment edit, not the diff's: it is still drawn from a file of the (line-scoped) pool and must not be passed through `drawable`, and this group owes the check that a pool of one touched site still carries it. The control for (2): #1565's first CI run (job 107650201671) started stress.py beside three shared drivers and its baseline hit the 1200 s per-driver timeout (rc=124, INCONCLUSIVE, no mutant scored), where serial baselines in jobs 107480454242 and 107577763331 took 960 s and 950 s. The control for the null control's cost: CI jobs 107531573572 (PR #1558) and 107541603524 (PR #1561, at 1b1dac86) drove the same ten mutants with the same killers on the same runner class, and only the second carried the null control; its mutant phase was the longer by about one full sweep. Re-measure: diff the timestamps between each log's last `baseline` line and its `survivor(s) of` line.
